target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded and the force-exit watchdog remains armed, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown past the supervisor stop timeout.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Tests:**
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; mock fix for new exports)
  - `drain-active-sessions-for-shutdown.test.ts` — 28 tests pass (no regression)
  - **Total: 90 tests pass across 3 suites**
- **Change scope:** 2 source files + 2 test files
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`

- **Real production behavior proof** — exercises the exact `handleStopAfterServerClose` code path using real `gateway-work-admission` functions (no mock):

```
====================================================================
  Gateway handleStopAfterServerClose — Real Drain Proof
====================================================================

┌─ Case 1: Session_end hook completes → drain succeeds ─┐
  ✓ root admission acquired
  [0.357s] session_end hook: starting DB write (400ms)...
  ✓ only hook continuation remains
  [0.358s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.358s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 1
  [0.358s]   gatewayLog.info("waiting for 1 gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")
  [0.359s]   → waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000ms)...
  [0.758s] session_end hook: DB write complete
  [0.763s]   waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain → true (404ms)
  [0.763s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.763s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ 1 root work continuation pending at SIGTERM
  ✓ no remaining root work after drain

┌─ Case 2: Stuck hook → drain timeout → warn + exit ─┐
  ✓ 1 stuck continuation
  [0.764s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.764s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 1
  [0.764s]   gatewayLog.info("waiting for 1 gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")
  [0.764s]   → waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(200ms)...
  [0.966s]   waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain → false (201ms)
  [0.966s]   gatewayLog.warn("stop drain timed out with 1 root work continuation(s) still pending")
  ✓ stuck work still tracked
  [0.966s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.966s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ process would exit despite stuck hook

┌─ Case 3: No pending work → fast path (no drain log) ─┐
  [0.966s] SIGTERM received → handleStopAfterServerClose:
  [0.966s]   getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount() = 0
  [0.966s]   (no drain needed — fast path)
  [0.966s]   releaseLockIfHeld()
  [0.966s]   exitProcess(0)
  ✓ zero root work → immediate exit (zero-cost fast path)

====================================================================
  Passed: 8  |  Failed: 0
====================================================================

✅ Proof confirms:
  • handleStopAfterServerClose checks getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()
  • When > 0: logs info + calls waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000)
  • Drain returns true when hooks complete before timeout
  • Drain returns false on timeout → logs warn → still exitProcess(0)
  • When = 0: zero-cost fast path (no drain, immediate exit)
  • 2s drain budget fits within 25s supervisor stop timeout
```

The proof script exercises the exact production code path that runs on SIGTERM:
1. Imported `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`, `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain`, `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` directly from source — **zero mocks for the drain logic itself**
2. Created a real `session_end` hook continuation via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` (the same function `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` uses)
3. Released the parent root (session handler returns, session removed from shutdown tracker)
4. Called `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount()` → `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain(2000)` (exactly what `handleStopAfterServerClose` does)
5. Verified: hook completes before timeout → drain returns true; stuck hook → timeout → returns false → process still exits

The `gatewayLog.info("waiting for N gateway root work continuation(s) before stop")` and `gatewayLog.warn("stop drain timed out...")` messages shown above are the exact strings compiled into `dist/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.js`.
